caption:
Claude now writes code so fast that Anthropic outgrew Git.
The company went from about 2,500 merged code changes a day in May to over 30,000 a day in September.
Its answer is Scion, a new in-house source control system built with help from Claude.

slides.headline: Claude writes so much code that Anthropic had to *replace Git* to keep up

slides.heading: From 2,500 to *30,000 a day*
paras: Anthropic says it averaged about 2,500 merged code changes per day in May 2026. By September, it was merging over 30,000 per day.
Its new engineering post says that jump comes from Claude writing more and more of the company's code.

slides.heading: Git *could not keep up*
paras: The main branch is about 100 GB. Anthropic runs roughly 25 million code checkouts a day just for testing.
Fetching that naively with Git would mean over 600 petabytes of traffic per day, the company estimates.

slides.heading: Meet *Scion*
paras: Scion is Anthropic's new centralized source control system. A seven-person team built it, and the move away from Git took five months.
Claude Mythos Preview rewrote an early part of it, making it use 20 times less memory and run four times faster.

slides.heading: Engineers who *say no*
paras: "Very often, we found that the role of the engineers was to tell Claude 'no,'" Anthropic wrote.

paras.t: Anthropic says demand for merging code is "practically infinite." Scion will not be open sourced.

slides.hook: Anthropic is now merging 30,000 changes a day. Follow to see what happens when every company codes this fast.
